hypotheses.reasoning: POST /login 503s come from account-svc, which fails because auth-svc (POST /tokens) is overloaded and load-shedding. The trigger appears to be auth-svc-3 failing its liveness probe and restarting at 12:06:48 (#1337), leaving capacity at 3/4. Immediately afterward account-svc begins retrying POST /tokens on 503 with zero delay (#1346 retry 2/4 delay 0ms, #1438 're-sending at once, no backoff policy', #1503 'backoff disabled'). Those retries multiply the request volume. auth-svc then reports 713-752 inflight, 3-5x baseline (#1397, #1544, #1639), and sheds load with 'queue full' (#1441, #1666, #2225). The edge then returns 503 on /login after retries are exhausted (#1376). The recovery stays stuck because the retry storm keeps the load above capacity. The S3 503s in catalog-svc, the search 500s, the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller and the account-svc heap warning are separate or unrelated and do not explain the login path. The specific reason auth-svc-3 failed its liveness probe is not visible in the logs.

Alternative reading: auth-svc-3 hit a resource problem (liveness failure and restart) that reduced capacity and started the overload. The logs show no memory or CPU error on auth-svc itself (GC pauses are normal, heap about 30-45%), so this is weakly supported. The account-svc heap warning at 12:03:39 is recovered and is unlikely to be the cause.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget to account-svc's AuthClient, and stop the immediate retries. Shed or rate-limit the retry traffic so auth-svc can drain its queue. Confirm auth-svc has returned to 4/4 healthy instances and check why auth-svc-3's liveness probe failed (its resource usage, and whether it was starved by the traffic before the restart). Then re-enable traffic gradually.

hypotheses.reasoning: POST /login 503s come from account-svc, which fails because auth-svc (POST /tokens) is overloaded and load-shedding. The trigger appears to be auth-svc-3 failing its liveness probe and restarting at 12:06:48 (#1337), leaving capacity at 3/4. Immediately afterward account-svc begins retrying POST /tokens on 503 with zero delay (#1346 retry 2/4 delay 0ms, #1438 're-sending at once, no backoff policy', #1503 'backoff disabled'). Those retries multiply the request volume. auth-svc then reports 713-752 inflight, 3-5x baseline (#1397, #1544, #1639), and sheds load with 'queue full' (#1441, #1666, #2225). The edge then returns 503 on /login after retries are exhausted (#1376). The recovery stays stuck because the retry storm keeps the load above capacity. The S3 503s in catalog-svc, the search 500s, the legacy-inventory healthcheck timeouts in status-poller and the account-svc heap warning are separate or unrelated and do not explain the login path. The specific reason auth-svc-3 failed its liveness probe is not visible in the logs.
hypotheses.recommendedAction: Immediately add exponential backoff with jitter and a retry budget to account-svc's AuthClient, and stop the immediate retries. Shed or rate-limit the retry traffic so auth-svc can drain its queue. Confirm auth-svc has returned to 4/4 healthy instances and check why auth-svc-3's liveness probe failed (its resource usage, and whether it was starved by the traffic before the restart). Then re-enable traffic gradually.
